<pasted_content id="8e83">
Closes #63

What: Adds a Duplicate action for promotions. It's in the row menu on the Promotions list and in the menu on the promotion detail page. It opens a drawer asking for the new code, pre-filled with <code>-COPY. Submitting creates the copy, shows a toast and takes you to the new promotion. If the code is already taken, the error shows on the code field and nothing is created.

Why: Running a similar promotion meant re-entering every setting and condition by hand.

How: It follows Logan's duplicate product work in #82. The form opens in a drawer, like the other small forms in the dashboard. A new duplicatePromotionWorkflow loads the original, checks the new code isn't taken, and creates the copy with createPromotionsWorkflow. The copy keeps the original's settings, discount and all of its conditions, target rules and buy rules, but it always starts as a draft with a usage count of 0. Its rules are created as new rules, so editing one promotion doesn't change the other, and it isn't added to the original's campaign. The reasoning is in the Design section on #63. I also added metadata to the CreatePromotionDTO type, since the model and module already support it but the type was missing it.

Testing: The tests are in the first two commits, before the code, and they failed before it because the route, the drawer and the menu actions didn't exist yet.

Integration tests cover a full duplicate (settings and rules copied, draft status, usage reset, no campaign), a buyget promotion's buy rules and quantities, the copy having its own rules, a code that's already taken, and a promotion that doesn't exist.
Dashboard tests cover the Duplicate action in both menus and the drawer: the pre-filled code, a successful duplicate and a taken code.
To run them:
yarn workspace @medusajs/dashboard test promotion-duplicate promotion-list-actions promotion-general-section
yarn build, then with Postgres running: cd integration-tests/http && DB_HOST=localhost DB_PORT=5433 DB_USERNAME=postgres DB_PASSWORD=postgres npx jest tests/promotions/admin/ (use your own DB_PORT)

All of them pass, along with the existing promotion integration tests, and the dashboard typecheck is clean. The full dashboard suite has one failure, "en.json should not have extra keys", which already fails on develop.

CI doesn't run on PRs in this repo, so the local runs above stand in for it.

Tech Debt
Introduced: The copy is built from a hand-written list of fields, so a field added to promotions later won't be copied until the list is updated.

Encountered: The admin API can't set a promotion's metadata, so the integration test sets it directly in the database to check it gets copied.

This is the issue:

<pasted_content id="8e83">
User Story
As a store admin, I want to duplicate an existing promotion so that I can launch a similar promotion without re-entering every rule and setting by hand.

User Scenario
User runs a "SUMMER20" promotion: 20% off orders over $50 for customers in the "Newsletter" group, limited to shirts. They want the same deal for a fall sale under a new code. In the admin dashboard they open Promotions, open the "SUMMER20" row menu and click "Duplicate." A dialog asks for the new code, with "SUMMER20-COPY" filled in. They enter "FALL20" and confirm. They land on the new promotion's detail page. It has the same type, discount value, conditions and target items as SUMMER20, but it is in Draft status and its usage count is 0. They review it and activate it when the sale starts.

Acceptance Criteria
The promotion list row menu and the promotion detail page both have a "Duplicate" action.
Choosing "Duplicate" opens a dialog asking for a new promotion code, pre-filled with <original code>-COPY.
Submitting the dialog creates a new promotion with the same type, automatic/manual setting, tax-inclusive setting, usage limit, metadata and application method (type, target type, allocation, value, currency, max quantity). It also copies all conditions, including target and buy rules.
The new promotion always starts in Draft status with a usage count of 0, whatever the original's status and usage.
Entering a code that another promotion already uses shows a validation error, and nothing is created.
After a successful duplicate, the admin is taken to the new promotion's detail page and sees a success toast.
Changing the copy afterwards does not affect the original, and changing the original does not affect the copy.
The duplicate logic lives in a core-flows workflow behind an admin API route (for example POST /admin/promotions/:id/duplicate).
Integration tests cover a successful duplicate (all fields and rules copied, status and usage reset) and a duplicate-code error. Dashboard tests cover the menu action and dialog.
Out of Scope
Duplicating several promotions at once.
Duplicating campaigns or campaign budgets.
Changing other fields in the duplicate dialog (only the code can be changed there; everything else is edited afterwards).
Open Questions
If the original belongs to a campaign, should the copy join the same campaign, which shares its budget, or be created without one?
Should the copy carry over the original's start and end dates, or clear them since they are probably outdated?
Design
Decision: Add a duplicatePromotionWorkflow that loads the original, checks the new code isn't taken, and creates the copy with createPromotionsWorkflow, the same way the duplicate product workflow does. The copy is created without a campaign, and its conditions, target rules and buy rules are created as new rules instead of being shared with the original.
Alternatives considered: (1) keep the original's campaign on the copy, (2) link the copy to the original's existing rule rows, since rules are many-to-many.
Rationale: (1) would make the copy share the original's campaign budget, so uses of the copy would count against it, and duplicating campaigns is out of scope. (2) would mean editing a condition on one promotion changes the other, which breaks AC7.
Consequences: The copy has no start or end dates, since those live on the campaign, so this also answers the second open question. The admin adds the copy to a campaign afterwards if they want one. Like the product duplicate, the copy is a hand-written list of fields, so a field added to promotions later won't be copied until the list is updated.
</pasted_content id="8e83">

+import {
+  AdditionalData,
+  CreatePromotionDTO,
+  CreatePromotionRuleDTO,
+} from "@medusajs/framework/types"
+import { MedusaError, PromotionStatus } from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
+import {
+  WorkflowData,
+  WorkflowResponse,
+  createStep,
+  createWorkflow,
+  transform,
+} from "@medusajs/framework/workflows-sdk"
+import { useQueryGraphStep } from "../../common"
+import { createPromotionsWorkflow } from "./create-promotions"
+
+/**
+ * The fields read from the original promotion, including its rules and their
+ * values.
+ */
+const DUPLICATE_PROMOTION_FIELDS = [
+  "id",
+  "type",
+  "is_automatic",
+  "is_tax_inclusive",
+  "limit",
+  "metadata",
+  "rules.description",
+  "rules.attribute",
+  "rules.operator",
+  "rules.values.value",
+  "application_method.type",
+  "application_method.target_type",
+  "application_method.allocation",
+  "application_method.value",
+  "application_method.currency_code",
+  "application_method.max_quantity",
+  "application_method.apply_to_quantity",
+  "application_method.buy_rules_min_quantity",
+  "application_method.target_rules.description",
+  "application_method.target_rules.attribute",
+  "application_method.target_rules.operator",
+  "application_method.target_rules.values.value",
+  "application_method.buy_rules.description",
+  "application_method.buy_rules.attribute",
+  "application_method.buy_rules.operator",
+  "application_method.buy_rules.values.value",
+]
+
+/**
+ * The data to duplicate a promotion, along with custom data that's passed to
+ * the hooks of the underlying create workflow.
+ */
+export type DuplicatePromotionWorkflowInput = {
+  /**
+   * The ID of the promotion to duplicate.
+   */
+  id: string
+  /**
+   * The code of the new promotion. It must not be used by another promotion.
+   */
+  code: string
+} & AdditionalData
+
+/**
+ * The data to validate before duplicating a promotion.
+ */
+export interface ValidateDuplicatePromotionStepInput {
+  /**
+   * The promotions matching the requested ID (empty if it does not exist).
+   */
+  source: { id: string }[]
+  /**
+   * The promotions already using the requested code.
+   */
+  codeConflicts: { id: string }[]
+  /**
+   * The requested code for the copy.
+   */
+  code: string
+}
+
+export const validateDuplicatePromotionStepId = "validate-duplicate-promotion"
+/**
+ * This step validates a duplicate request. It throws if the original promotion
+ * is missing or if the code is already used by another promotion, before
+ * anything is created.
+ */
+export const validateDuplicatePromotionStep = createStep(
+  validateDuplicatePromotionStepId,
+  async (data: ValidateDuplicatePromotionStepInput) => {
+    if (!data.source[0]) {
+      throw new MedusaError(
+        MedusaError.Types.NOT_FOUND,
+        "Promotion to duplicate was not found"
+      )
+    }
+
+    // Same message as the create API gives for a code that's taken.
+    if (data.codeConflicts.length) {
+      throw new MedusaError(
+        MedusaError.Types.INVALID_DATA,
+        `Promotion with code: ${data.code}, already exists.`
+      )
+    }
+  }
+)
+
+/**
+ * Copies rules as new rules, so the copy doesn't share rule rows with the
+ * original.
+ */
+const copyRules = (rules?: Record<string, any>[]): CreatePromotionRuleDTO[] =>
+  (rules ?? []).map((rule) => ({
+    description: rule.description,
+    attribute: rule.attribute,
+    operator: rule.operator,
+    values: rule.values.map((value: { value: string }) => value.value),
+  }))
+
+/**
+ * Maps a loaded promotion to the input of `createPromotionsWorkflow`. The copy
+ * always starts as a draft with no usage, and it isn't added to the original's
+ * campaign.
+ */
+export const buildDuplicatePromotionInput = (
+  source: Record<string, any>,
+  code: string
+): CreatePromotionDTO => {
+  const method = source.application_method
+
+  return {
+    code,
+    type: source.type,
+    status: PromotionStatus.DRAFT,
+    is_automatic: source.is_automatic,
+    is_tax_inclusive: source.is_tax_inclusive,
+    limit: source.limit,
+    metadata: source.metadata,
+    rules: copyRules(source.rules),
+    application_method: {
+      type: method.type,
+      target_type: method.target_type,
+      allocation: method.allocation,
+      value: method.value,
+      currency_code: method.currency_code,
+      max_quantity: method.max_quantity,
+      apply_to_quantity: method.apply_to_quantity,
+      buy_rules_min_quantity: method.buy_rules_min_quantity,
+      target_rules: copyRules(method.target_rules),
+      buy_rules: copyRules(method.buy_rules),
+    },
+  }
+}
+
+export const duplicatePromotionWorkflowId = "duplicate-promotion"
+/**
+ * This workflow duplicates a promotion, including its conditions, target rules
+ * and buy rules. It's used by the Duplicate Promotion Admin API Route.
+ *
+ * The copy always starts as a draft with a usage count of 0, its rules are new
+ * rules rather than shared with the original, and it isn't added to the
+ * original's campaign.
+ *
+ * @example
+ * const { result } = await duplicatePromotionWorkflow(container)
+ * .run({
+ *   input: {
+ *     id: "promo_123",
+ *     code: "FALL20",
+ *   }
+ * })
+ *
+ * @summary
+ *
+ * Duplicate a promotion with its rules.
+ */
+export const duplicatePromotionWorkflow = createWorkflow(
+  duplicatePromotionWorkflowId,
+  (input: WorkflowData<DuplicatePromotionWorkflowInput>) => {
+    const { data: source } = useQueryGraphStep({
+      entity: "promotion",
+      fields: DUPLICATE_PROMOTION_FIELDS,
+      filters: { id: input.id },
+    }).config({ name: "get-promotion-to-duplicate" })
+
+    const { data: codeConflicts } = useQueryGraphStep({
+      entity: "promotion",
+      fields: ["id"],
+      filters: { code: input.code },
+    }).config({ name: "get-promotions-with-code" })
+
+    validateDuplicatePromotionStep({
+      source,
+      codeConflicts,
+      code: input.code,
+    })
+
+    const promotionsData = transform({ source, input }, (data) => [
+      buildDuplicatePromotionInput(data.source[0], data.input.code),
+    ])
+
+    const created = createPromotionsWorkflow.runAsStep({
+      input: {
+        promotionsData,
+        additional_data: input.additional_data,
+      },
+    })
+
+    return new WorkflowResponse(created)
+  }
+)

+import { duplicatePromotionWorkflow } from "@medusajs/core-flows"
+import {
+  AuthenticatedMedusaRequest,
+  MedusaResponse,

+import { AdditionalData, HttpTypes } from "@medusajs/framework/types"

+export const POST = async (

+    input: { id: req.params.id, code, additional_data },
+  })
+
+  const promotion = await refetchPromotion(
+    result[0].id,
+    req.scope,
+    req.queryConfig.fields
+  )
+
+  res.status(200).json({ promotion })
+}

+import { HttpTypes } from "@medusajs/types"
+import { Button, Input, toast } from "@medusajs/ui"
+import { FieldErrors, Resolver, useForm } from "react-hook-form"
+import { useTranslation } from "react-i18next"
+
+import { Form } from "../../../../../components/common/form"
+import { RouteDrawer, useRouteModal } from "../../../../../components/modals"
+import { KeyboundForm } from "../../../../../components/utilities/keybound-form"
+import { useDuplicatePromotion } from "../../../../../hooks/api/promotions"
+
+type DuplicatePromotionFormProps = {
+  promotion: Pick<HttpTypes.AdminPromotion, "id" | "code">
+}
+
+type DuplicatePromotionValues = { code: string }
+
+/**
+ * The code is required, nothing else is checked here. The server checks that
+ * no other promotion uses it, and that error is shown on the field.
+ *
+ * This is a plain resolver instead of `zodResolver` for the same reason as the
+ * duplicate product form: the installed `@hookform/resolvers` can't catch zod 4
+ * validation errors.
+ */
+const resolver: Resolver<DuplicatePromotionValues> = async (values) => {
+  const code = values.code.trim()
+  const errors: FieldErrors<DuplicatePromotionValues> = {}
+
+  if (!code) {
+    errors.code = { type: "required", message: "" }
+  }
+
+  return Object.keys(errors).length
+    ? { values: {}, errors }
+    : { values: { code }, errors: {} }
+}
+
+export const DuplicatePromotionForm = ({
+  promotion,
+}: DuplicatePromotionFormProps) => {
+  const { t } = useTranslation()
+  const { handleSuccess } = useRouteModal()
+
+  const form = useForm<DuplicatePromotionValues>({
+    defaultValues: {
+      code: `${promotion.code}-COPY`,
+    },
+    resolver,
+  })
+
+  const { mutateAsync, isPending } = useDuplicatePromotion(promotion.id)
+
+  const handleSubmit = form.handleSubmit(async (data) => {
+    await mutateAsync(
+      { code: data.code },
+      {
+        onSuccess: ({ promotion: created }) => {
+          toast.success(
+            t("promotions.duplicate.successToast", { code: created.code })
+          )
+          // Land on the new draft promotion, not the original. Going through
+          // handleSuccess skips the unsaved changes prompt for an edited code.
+          handleSuccess(`/promotions/${created.id}`)
+        },
+        onError: (e) => {
+          // e.g. another promotion already uses the code.
+          form.setError("code", { type: "manual", message: e.message })
+        },
+      }
+    )
+  })
+
+  return (
+    <RouteDrawer.Form form={form}>
+      <KeyboundForm
+        onSubmit={handleSubmit}
+        className="flex flex-1 flex-col overflow-hidden"
+      >
+        <RouteDrawer.Body className="flex flex-1 flex-col gap-y-4 overflow-y-auto">
+          <Form.Field
+            control={form.control}
+            name="code"
+            render={({ field }) => {
+              return (
+                <Form.Item>
+                  <Form.Label>{t("fields.code")}</Form.Label>
+                  <Form.Control>
+                    <Input {...field} />
+                  </Form.Control>
+                  <Form.ErrorMessage />
+                </Form.Item>
+              )
+            }}
+          />
+        </RouteDrawer.Body>
+        <RouteDrawer.Footer>
+          <div className="flex items-center justify-end gap-x-2">
+            <RouteDrawer.Close asChild>
+              <Button size="small" variant="secondary">
+                {t("actions.cancel")}
+              </Button>
+            </RouteDrawer.Close>
+            <Button size="small" type="submit" isLoading={isPending}>
+              {t("actions.duplicate")}
+            </Button>
+          </div>
+        </RouteDrawer.Footer>
+      </KeyboundForm>
+    </RouteDrawer.Form>
+  )
+}

+import { Heading } from "@medusajs/ui"
+import { useTranslation } from "react-i18next"
+import { useParams } from "react-router-dom"
+
+import { RouteDrawer } from "../../../components/modals"
+import { usePromotion } from "../../../hooks/api/promotions"
+import { DuplicatePromotionForm } from "./components/duplicate-promotion-form"
+
+export const PromotionDuplicate = () => {
+  const { id } = useParams()
+  const { t } = useTranslation()
+
+  const { promotion, isLoading, isError, error } = usePromotion(id!)
+
+  if (isError) {
+    throw error
+  }
+
+  return (
+    <RouteDrawer>
+      <RouteDrawer.Header>
+        <RouteDrawer.Title asChild>
+          <Heading>{t("promotions.duplicate.header")}</Heading>
+        </RouteDrawer.Title>
+        <RouteDrawer.Description>
+          {t("promotions.duplicate.description")}
+        </RouteDrawer.Description>
+      </RouteDrawer.Header>
+      {!isLoading && promotion && (
+        <DuplicatePromotionForm promotion={promotion} />
+      )}
+    </RouteDrawer>
+  )
+}

<pasted_content id="8e83">
Summary
What — What changes are introduced in this PR?

Adds a "Duplicate" action for products (closes #65). From the product detail page or a product list row menu, an admin opens a drawer that asks for a title and handle, pre-filled with <title> (Copy) and <handle>-copy. Submitting creates a copy and redirects to it with a success toast. The original is unchanged.

The copy is always a draft and includes the original's options, option values, variants, prices (every currency and region), images, thumbnail, product type, collection, categories, tags, sales channels, shipping profile, dimensions, weight, discountable flag and metadata. Variant SKU, barcode, EAN and UPC are left empty. Stock levels are not copied: variants that manage inventory get new inventory items with no stock.

Why — Why are these changes relevant or necessary?

Store owners who sell near-identical products (for example a "Classic Tee" with 12 variants and prices in two currencies) currently have to rebuild options, variants and prices by hand. Duplicating removes that repetitive work.

How — How have these changes been implemented?

Workflow (core-flows, duplicate-product.ts): loads the source product in one query, validates the request, maps it to a create payload and runs it through createProductsWorkflow. Validation runs before anything is created, so a failed request leaves no data behind.
API route: POST /admin/products/:id/duplicate with body { title, handle }, behind the same permissions as creating a product. It also adds the validator, the AdminDuplicateProduct type and a sdk.admin.product.duplicate() method in the JS SDK.
Dashboard: a useDuplicateProduct hook, a new product-duplicate route (drawer and form), the Duplicate menu item in both menus, and en.json strings.
Open questions from the issue, resolved: images point at the same file URLs as the original (so deleting an image file from one product can affect the other), SKUs are left empty rather than suffixed, and there is no cap or warning for products with many variants.
Testing — How have these changes been tested, or how can the reviewer test the feature?

Integration spec integration-tests/http/__tests__/product/admin/product-duplicate.spec.ts (7 tests, passing): full duplicate (options, variants, prices, relations copied, unique fields cleared, draft status), original unchanged, new inventory items with no stock, duplicate handle returns 400 and creates nothing, the pre-filled "(Copy)" title and handle are accepted, an empty title returns 400, and an unknown product returns 404.
Dashboard unit tests for the form (4 tests, passing): pre-fill, submitting the pre-filled values, submitting edited values, and an emptied title not submitting.
The packages the backend depends on build cleanly, which type-checks the workflow, route, types, SDK and dashboard changes.
Also manually verified, can confirm on the dashboard
Examples
Provide examples or code snippets that demonstrate how this feature works, or how it can be used in practice.
This helps with documentation and ensures maintainers can quickly understand and verify the change.

// Admin JS SDK
const { product } = await sdk.admin.product.duplicate("prod_123", {
  title: "Classic Tee - Long Sleeve",
  handle: "classic-tee-long-sleeve",
})
// product.status === "draft"; variants have no sku, barcode, ean or upc

// HTTP
// POST /admin/products/prod_123/duplicate
// { "title": "Classic Tee - Long Sleeve", "handle": "classic-tee-long-sleeve" }
// 200 -> { product }
// 400 -> empty title, or handle already in use
// 404 -> source product not found

// Workflow, for use in custom code
import { duplicateProductWorkflow } from "@medusajs/core-flows"

const { result } = await duplicateProductWorkflow(container).run({
  input: {
    id: "prod_123",
    title: "Classic Tee - Long Sleeve",
    handle: "classic-tee-long-sleeve",
  },
})
Checklist
Please ensure the following before requesting a review:

I have added a changeset for this PR
The changes are covered by relevant tests
I have verified the code works as intended locally
I have linked the related issue(s) if applicable

Additional Context
Decisions: The drawer validates its fields with a small hand-written resolver that only requires a non-empty title and handle. The alternative is the repo's usual zodResolver. @hookform/resolvers can't catch zod 4 errors, so the rejection would be left as unhandled. This is off the repo's pattern, and leaves the underlying mismatch in place, but allows for correct error handling in this implementation.

Tech Debt
Introduced: The copy is a hand-written field lift, so any field added to the model later will be silently left off the copy.

Encountered: None encountered.

Issue:

<pasted_content id="8e83">
User Story
As a store admin, I want to duplicate an existing product so that I can quickly add similar products without rebuilding their options, variants and prices from scratch.

User Scenario
An admin sells a "Classic Tee" with 3 colors and 4 sizes, which makes 12 variants, each with prices in USD and EUR. They are adding a "Classic Tee - Long Sleeve" that has the same structure. They open Classic Tee in the admin dashboard and click "Duplicate" in the actions menu. A dialog asks for a title and handle, pre-filled with "Classic Tee (Copy)" and "classic-tee-copy." They change them to "Classic Tee - Long Sleeve" and "classic-tee-long-sleeve" and confirm. They land on the new draft product, which has all 12 variants, prices, images, categories and sales channels already set up. They raise the prices, replaces the images and publishes it.

Acceptance Criteria
The product detail page actions menu and the product list row menu both have a "Duplicate" action.
Choosing "Duplicate" opens a dialog asking for title and handle, pre-filled with <title> (Copy) and <handle>-copy.
The new product copies subtitle, description, images, thumbnail, product type, collection, categories, tags, sales channels, shipping profile, dimensions and weight, discountable flag and metadata.
Options and option values are copied. Every variant is copied with its title, option values, inventory management settings, dimensions, metadata and prices in every currency and region.
Variant fields that must be unique (SKU, barcode, EAN, UPC) are left empty on the copy.
The new product always starts in Draft status, whatever the original's status.
Stock levels are not copied. Copied variants that manage inventory get new inventory items with no stock.
A handle already used by another product shows a validation error, and nothing is created.
After a successful duplicate, the admin is taken to the new product's detail page and sees a success toast. The original is unchanged.
The logic lives in a core-flows workflow that reuses createProductsWorkflow, behind an admin API route (for example POST /admin/products/:id/duplicate).
Integration tests cover a full duplicate (options, variants, prices, relations copied; unique fields cleared; draft status) and a duplicate-handle error. Dashboard tests cover the menu action and dialog.
Out of Scope
Duplicating several products at once.
Copying stock levels or reservations.
Copying translations.
Choosing which parts to copy (it's all or nothing).
Open Questions
Should images be re-uploaded as new files, or should the copy point at the same file URLs? Pointing at the same files is simpler, but deleting an image from one product could break the other.
Should SKUs be cleared, or set automatically to something like <original SKU>-COPY?
Should products with a very large number of variants have a cap or a warning?
</pasted_content id="8e83">

+++ b/packages/core/core-flows/src/product/workflows/duplicate-product.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,303 @@
+import {
+  AdditionalData,
+  CreateProductWorkflowInputDTO,
+} from "@medusajs/framework/types"
+import { MedusaError } from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
+import {
+  WorkflowData,
+  WorkflowResponse,
+  createStep,
+  createWorkflow,
+  transform,
+} from "@medusajs/framework/workflows-sdk"
+import { useQueryGraphStep } from "../../common"
+import { createProductsWorkflow } from "./create-products"
+
+/**
+ * The fields read from the source product. Everything the duplicate needs is
+ * fetched in one query, including nested options, variants and prices.
+ */
+const DUPLICATE_PRODUCT_FIELDS = [
+  "id",
+  "title",
+  "handle",
+  "subtitle",
+  "description",
+  "is_giftcard",
+  "discountable",
+  "thumbnail",
+  "weight",
+  "length",
+  "height",
+  "width",
+  "hs_code",
+  "origin_country",
+  "mid_code",
+  "material",
+  "metadata",
+  "type_id",
+  "collection_id",
+  "images.url",
+  "images.metadata",
+  "options.title",
+  "options.values.value",
+  "tags.id",
+  "categories.id",
+  "sales_channels.id",
+  "shipping_profile.id",
+  "variants.title",
+  "variants.manage_inventory",
+  "variants.allow_backorder",
+  "variants.variant_rank",
+  "variants.weight",
+  "variants.length",
+  "variants.height",
+  "variants.width",
+  "variants.hs_code",
+  "variants.origin_country",
+  "variants.mid_code",
+  "variants.material",
+  "variants.metadata",
+  "variants.options.value",
+  "variants.options.option.title",
+  "variants.prices.amount",
+  "variants.prices.currency_code",
+  "variants.prices.min_quantity",
+  "variants.prices.max_quantity",
+  "variants.prices.price_rules.attribute",
+  "variants.prices.price_rules.value",
+]
+
+/**
+ * The data to duplicate a product, along with custom data that's passed to the
+ * hooks of the underlying create workflow.
+ */
+export type DuplicateProductWorkflowInput = {
+  /**
+   * The ID of the product to duplicate.
+   */
+  id: string
+  /**
+   * The title of the new product.
+   */
+  title: string
+  /**
+   * The handle of the new product. It must not be used by another product.
+   */
+  handle: string
+} & AdditionalData
+
+/**
+ * The data to validate before duplicating a product.
+ */
+export interface ValidateDuplicateProductStepInput {
+  /**
+   * The products matching the requested ID (empty if it does not exist).
+   */
+  source: { id: string }[]
+  /**
+   * The products already using the requested handle.
+   */
+  handleConflicts: { id: string }[]
+  /**
+   * The requested handle for the copy.
+   */
+  handle: string
+}
+
+const validateDuplicateProductStepId = "validate-duplicate-product"
+/**
+ * This step validates a duplicate request. It throws if the source product is
+ * missing or if the handle is already used by another product. Running it
+ * before anything is created means a failed validation leaves no data behind.
+ */
+export const validateDuplicateProductStep = createStep(
+  validateDuplicateProductStepId,
+  async (data: ValidateDuplicateProductStepInput) => {
+    const [source] = data.source
+
+    if (!source) {
+      throw new MedusaError(
+        MedusaError.Types.NOT_FOUND,
+        "Product to duplicate was not found"
+      )
+    }
+
+    if (data.handleConflicts.length) {
+      throw new MedusaError(
+        MedusaError.Types.INVALID_DATA,
+        `Product with handle "${data.handle}" already exists.`
+      )
+    }
+  }
+)
+
+/**
+ * The data to build the create payload for the copy.
+ */
+export interface BuildDuplicateProductInputStepInput {
+  /**
+   * The fully loaded source product.
+   */
+  source: Record<string, any>
+  /**
+   * The title of the copy.
+   */
+  title: string
+  /**
+   * The handle of the copy.
+   */
+  handle: string
+}
+
+/**
+ * Maps a loaded product to the input of `createProductsWorkflow`.
+ *
+ * This is a plain function (used inside `transform`) so it stays easy to
+ * unit test. Unique variant fields (sku, barcode, ean, upc) are deliberately
+ * never copied, and the copy always starts as a draft.
+ */
+export const buildDuplicateProductInput = (
+  data: BuildDuplicateProductInputStepInput
+): CreateProductWorkflowInputDTO => {
+  const { source } = data
+
+  return {
+    title: data.title.trim(),
+    handle: data.handle,
+    // A copy is never published automatically, whatever the original is.
+    status: "draft",
+    subtitle: source.subtitle,
+    description: source.description,
+    is_giftcard: source.is_giftcard,
+    discountable: source.discountable,
+    thumbnail: source.thumbnail,
+    // Images point at the same file URLs as the original.
+    images: (source.images ?? []).map((image: any) => ({
+      url: image.url,
+      metadata: image.metadata,
+    })),
+    weight: source.weight,
+    length: source.length,
+    height: source.height,
+    width: source.width,
+    hs_code: source.hs_code,
+    origin_country: source.origin_country,
+    mid_code: source.mid_code,
+    material: source.material,
+    metadata: source.metadata,
+    type_id: source.type_id,
+    collection_id: source.collection_id,
+    tag_ids: (source.tags ?? []).map((tag: any) => tag.id),
+    category_ids: (source.categories ?? []).map((category: any) => category.id),
+    sales_channels: (source.sales_channels ?? []).map((channel: any) => ({
+      id: channel.id,
+    })),
+    shipping_profile_id: source.shipping_profile?.id,
+    options: (source.options ?? []).map((option: any) => ({
+      title: option.title,
+      values: (option.values ?? []).map((value: any) => value.value),
+    })),
+    variants: (source.variants ?? []).map((variant: any) => ({
+      title: variant.title,
+      // sku, barcode, ean and upc are intentionally omitted: they must be
+      // unique, so they are left empty on the copy.
+      manage_inventory: variant.manage_inventory,
+      allow_backorder: variant.allow_backorder,
+      variant_rank: variant.variant_rank,
+      weight: variant.weight,
+      length: variant.length,
+      height: variant.height,
+      width: variant.width,
+      hs_code: variant.hs_code,
+      origin_country: variant.origin_country,
+      mid_code: variant.mid_code,
+      material: variant.material,
+      metadata: variant.metadata,
+      // { [option title]: option value }
+      options: Object.fromEntries(
+        (variant.options ?? []).map((value: any) => [
+          value.option?.title,
+          value.value,
+        ])
+      ),
+      // Every currency and region price is copied, including its rules.
+      prices: (variant.prices ?? []).map((price: any) => ({
+        amount: price.amount,
+        currency_code: price.currency_code,
+        min_quantity: price.min_quantity,
+        max_quantity: price.max_quantity,
+        rules: Object.fromEntries(
+          (price.price_rules ?? []).map((rule: any) => [
+            rule.attribute,
+            rule.value,
+          ])
+        ),
+      })),
+    })),
+  } as CreateProductWorkflowInputDTO
+}
+
+export const duplicateProductWorkflowId = "duplicate-product"
+/**
+ * This workflow duplicates a product, including its options, variants, prices
+ * and relations. It's used by the Duplicate Product Admin API Route.
+ *
+ * Unique variant fields (SKU, barcode, EAN, UPC) are left empty on the copy,
+ * the copy always starts as a draft, and stock levels are not copied: variants
+ * that manage inventory get new inventory items without stock, created by
+ * `createProductsWorkflow`.
+ *
+ * @example
+ * const { result } = await duplicateProductWorkflow(container)
+ * .run({
+ *   input: {
+ *     id: "prod_123",
+ *     title: "Classic Tee - Long Sleeve",
+ *     handle: "classic-tee-long-sleeve",
+ *   }
+ * })
+ *
+ * @summary
+ *
+ * Duplicate a product with its options, variants and prices.
+ */
+export const duplicateProductWorkflow = createWorkflow(
+  duplicateProductWorkflowId,
+  (input: WorkflowData<DuplicateProductWorkflowInput>) => {
+    const { data: source } = useQueryGraphStep({
+      entity: "product",
+      fields: DUPLICATE_PRODUCT_FIELDS,
+      filters: { id: input.id },
+    }).config({ name: "get-product-to-duplicate" })
+
+    const { data: handleConflicts } = useQueryGraphStep({
+      entity: "product",
+      fields: ["id"],
+      filters: { handle: input.handle },
+    }).config({ name: "get-products-with-handle" })
+
+    validateDuplicateProductStep({
+      source,
+      handleConflicts,
+      handle: input.handle,
+    })
+
+    const products = transform({ source, input }, (data) => [
+      buildDuplicateProductInput({
+        source: data.source[0],
+        title: data.input.title,
+        handle: data.input.handle,
+      }),
+    ])
+
+    const created = createProductsWorkflow.runAsStep({
+      input: {
+        products,
+        additional_data: input.additional_data,
+      },
+    })
+
+    return new WorkflowResponse(created)
+  }
+)

@@ -0,0 +1,33 @@
+import { duplicateProductWorkflow } from "@medusajs/core-flows"
+import {
+  AuthenticatedMedusaRequest,
+  MedusaResponse,
+  refetchEntity,
+} from "@medusajs/framework/http"
+import { AdditionalData, HttpTypes } from "@medusajs/framework/types"
+import { remapKeysForProduct, remapProductResponse } from "../../helpers"
+
+export const POST = async (
+  req: AuthenticatedMedusaRequest<
+    HttpTypes.AdminDuplicateProduct & AdditionalData,
+    HttpTypes.SelectParams
+  >,
+  res: MedusaResponse<HttpTypes.AdminProductResponse>
+) => {
+  const { title, handle, additional_data } = req.validatedBody
+
+  // The workflow validates the source product, the new title and the handle
+  // before creating anything, and throws a MedusaError otherwise.
+  const { result } = await duplicateProductWorkflow(req.scope).run({
+    input: { id: req.params.id, title, handle, additional_data },
+  })
+
+  const product = await refetchEntity({
+    entity: "product",
+    idOrFilter: result[0].id,
+    scope: req.scope,
+    fields: remapKeysForProduct(req.queryConfig.fields ?? []),
+  })
+
+  res.status(200).json({ product: remapProductResponse(product) })
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,134 @@
+import { HttpTypes } from "@medusajs/types"
+import { Button, Input, toast } from "@medusajs/ui"
+import { FieldErrors, Resolver, useForm } from "react-hook-form"
+import { useTranslation } from "react-i18next"
+import { useNavigate } from "react-router-dom"
+
+import { Form } from "../../../../../components/common/form"
+import { RouteDrawer } from "../../../../../components/modals"
+import { KeyboundForm } from "../../../../../components/utilities/keybound-form"
+import { useDuplicateProduct } from "../../../../../hooks/api/products"
+
+type DuplicateProductFormProps = {
+  product: Pick<HttpTypes.AdminProduct, "id" | "title" | "handle">
+}
+
+type DuplicateProductValues = { title: string; handle: string }
+
+/**
+ * Both fields are required, nothing else is checked here. The server still
+ * checks that the handle is not already used by another product and the error
+ * is shown as a toast.
+ *
+ * This is a plain resolver instead of `zodResolver` because the installed
+ * `@hookform/resolvers` (3.4.2) cannot catch zod 4 validation errors: it
+ * rethrows them, so an empty field would never show an error.
+ */
+const resolver: Resolver<DuplicateProductValues> = async (values) => {
+  const title = values.title.trim()
+  const handle = values.handle.trim()
+  const errors: FieldErrors<DuplicateProductValues> = {}
+
+  if (!title) {
+    errors.title = { type: "required", message: "" }
+  }
+
+  if (!handle) {
+    errors.handle = { type: "required", message: "" }
+  }
+
+  return Object.keys(errors).length
+    ? { values: {}, errors }
+    : { values: { title, handle }, errors: {} }
+}
+
+export const DuplicateProductForm = ({
+  product,
+}: DuplicateProductFormProps) => {
+  const { t } = useTranslation()
+  const navigate = useNavigate()
+
+  const form = useForm<DuplicateProductValues>({
+    // Pre-filled as a starting point; the owner can keep or edit both values.
+    defaultValues: {
+      title: `${product.title} (Copy)`,
+      handle: `${product.handle}-copy`,
+    },
+    resolver,
+  })
+
+  const { mutateAsync, isPending } = useDuplicateProduct(product.id)
+
+  const handleSubmit = form.handleSubmit(async (data) => {
+    await mutateAsync(
+      { title: data.title.trim(), handle: data.handle.trim() },
+      {
+        onSuccess: ({ product: created }) => {
+          toast.success(
+            t("products.duplicate.successToast", { title: created.title })
+          )
+          // Land on the new draft product, not the original.
+          navigate(`/products/${created.id}`, { replace: true })
+        },
+        onError: (e) => {
+          // e.g. the handle is already used by another product.
+          toast.error(e.message)
+        },
+      }
+    )
+  })
+
+  return (
+    <RouteDrawer.Form form={form}>
+      <KeyboundForm
+        onSubmit={handleSubmit}
+        className="flex flex-1 flex-col overflow-hidden"
+      >
+        <RouteDrawer.Body className="flex flex-1 flex-col gap-y-4 overflow-y-auto">
+          <Form.Field
+            control={form.control}
+            name="title"
+            render={({ field }) => {
+              return (
+                <Form.Item>
+                  <Form.Label>{t("fields.title")}</Form.Label>
+                  <Form.Control>
+                    <Input {...field} />
+                  </Form.Control>
+                  <Form.ErrorMessage />
+                </Form.Item>
+              )
+            }}
+          />
+          <Form.Field
+            control={form.control}
+            name="handle"
+            render={({ field }) => {
+              return (
+                <Form.Item>
+                  <Form.Label>{t("fields.handle")}</Form.Label>
+                  <Form.Control>
+                    <Input {...field} />
+                  </Form.Control>
+                  <Form.ErrorMessage />
+                </Form.Item>
+              )
+            }}
+          />
+        </RouteDrawer.Body>
+        <RouteDrawer.Footer>
+          <div className="flex items-center justify-end gap-x-2">
+            <RouteDrawer.Close asChild>
+              <Button size="small" variant="secondary">
+                {t("actions.cancel")}
+              </Button>
+            </RouteDrawer.Close>
+            <Button size="small" type="submit" isLoading={isPending}>
+              {t("actions.duplicate")}
+            </Button>
+          </div>
+        </RouteDrawer.Footer>
+      </KeyboundForm>
+    </RouteDrawer.Form>
+  )
+}

+import { Heading } from "@medusajs/ui"
+import { useTranslation } from "react-i18next"
+import { useParams } from "react-router-dom"
+
+import { RouteDrawer } from "../../../components/modals"
+import { useProduct } from "../../../hooks/api/products"
+import { DuplicateProductForm } from "./components/duplicate-product-form"
+
+export const ProductDuplicate = () => {
+  const { id } = useParams()
+  const { t } = useTranslation()
+
+  // Only the fields needed to pre-fill and validate the dialog are loaded.
+  const { product, isLoading, isError, error } = useProduct(id!, {
+    fields: "id,title,handle",
+  })
+
+  if (isError) {
+    throw error
+  }
+
+  return (
+    <RouteDrawer>
+      <RouteDrawer.Header>
+        <RouteDrawer.Title asChild>
+          <Heading>{t("products.duplicate.header")}</Heading>
+        </RouteDrawer.Title>
+        <RouteDrawer.Description>
+          {t("products.duplicate.description")}
+        </RouteDrawer.Description>
+      </RouteDrawer.Header>
+      {!isLoading && product && <DuplicateProductForm product={product} />}
+    </RouteDrawer>
+  )
+}

In [get-route.map.tsx:89-98](packages/admin/dashboard/src/dashboard-app/routes/get-route.map.tsx#L89-L98) the `duplicate` route and the `edit-all` route ended up in the same object, so the second `path`/`lazy` replaces the first. The `/products/:id/duplicate` route doesn't exist anymore, so the Duplicate menu items lead nowhere. The dashboard typecheck also fails now (`TS1117: An object literal cannot have multiple properties with the same name`). Splitting them back into two objects fixes it. |

The issue also asks for dashboard tests of the menu action, and there aren't any yet. A test that checks the Duplicate item in the list and detail menus would have caught the route problem above. |
| Code quality: consistent style, clear naming, no unnecessary duplication | 8 | Clean, readable workflow. Mapping the product in a plain function and reusing `createProductsWorkflow` works well, and the comments explain the choices. One small suggestion: a taken handle currently shows as a toast.
